strategy_objective_guidance:
- The evaluator (PRISM model-placement benchmark) runs the submitted `compute_model_placement` on test instances and scores the achieved **maximum KVPR across GPUs**, with hard constraints that (a) every model is placed on exactly one GPU and (b) `sum(model_size)` on each GPU ≤ `GPU_MEM_SIZE`. Placements violating memory or dropping/duplicating models are invalid (score zero / rejected), so feasibility dominates everything.
- The scored quantity is `max over GPUs of [ sum(req_rate/slo) / (GPU_MEM - sum(model_size)) ]`. Minimizing it means balancing the *ratio* load/mem-headroom, not just load: a GPU with more free memory tolerates more KV-cache pressure. Note the denominator makes the objective non-linear in placement — this is not plain balanced assignment.
- The full input (all models, all GPUs, all sizes/rates/SLOs) is given to the program at once, so **offline/batch/global optimization is fully permitted**; no causal or streaming assumption is needed. There is no runtime budget term visible beyond "executes correctly without errors" and "as simple as possible" (a soft preference, not scored).
- Terms that conflict: putting a model on a large-memory GPU lowers its denominator contribution but may starve other models of that headroom; memory-heavy models consume the denominator that reduces KVPR. The largest remaining lever is typically moving high `req_rate/slo` (high numerator) models onto GPUs with the most leftover memory — i.e., jointly packing sizes and rates rather than greedy-by-size.
- No term rewards anything contrary to the nominal goal; the best-scoring program is genuinely the best placement, subject to feasibility.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Greedy heuristics with different orderings: sort models by `req_rate/slo` descending (or by `req_rate/slo/model_size` pressure density) and assign each to the GPU that minimizes the resulting max-KVPR while fitting memory. Pure Python; no library needed.
- Local search / hill-climbing from a feasible start: repeatedly try single-model moves and pairwise swaps between GPUs, accept if the global max KVPR decreases (or a simulated-annealing schedule via `numpy.random`). This is the classic strong method for min-max partitioning.
- Metaheuristic global search: `scipy.optimize.dual_annealing` or `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` over an assignment encoding (e.g., a vector of GPU indices per model with a memory-feasibility repair/penalty). Works because the input is fully available offline.
- Bin-packing-style lower-bound reasoning: compute the LP-style lower bound on achievable max KVPR (total numerator / total usable memory) and use first-fit-decreasing on memory to guarantee feasibility, then rebalance.
- Multi-start randomized assignment: many random feasible starts (`numpy.random.permutation`), keep the best; cheap and robust for small instance sizes.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Improve the greedy tie-break: when choosing a GPU for a model, score candidate GPUs by resulting max KVPR *after* placement, not by current KVPR; iterate to a fixed point (relocate any model that lowers the max).
- Add a swap/move local-search polish loop after any constructor (greedy or random), run until no improving move exists or a fixed iteration cap (e.g., 2000 evaluations) — this reliably converts a mediocre feasible solution into a near-optimal one.
- Tune the ordering key: try `req_rate/slo`, `req_rate/slo/size`, and `size` orderings; pick per-instance by running all three and keeping the best placement.
- In annealing/DE, use a penalty proportional to memory overflow rather than hard rejection, so infeasible regions are explorable, then repair by moving oversized models to any GPU with room.
- Ensure determinism and simplicity: fixed random seeds, no external state, direct returns of the required data structure — preserves the "executes correctly" constraint and avoids evaluator-format mismatches.

strategies.title: [annealing-escape] Simulated annealing over assignment vector with memory-penalt
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Simulated annealing / stochastic global search over GPU-index encoding
Replacement scope: Replace the entire body of `compute_model_placement` (greedy constructor + local search) with: greedy construction for the feasible seed, then a simulated-annealing loop over an assignment vector `x[i] = gpu index of model i`.
Compute budget: ≤ 2000 annealing iterations per instance, single start, fixed seed (numpy default_rng(0)); expected evaluation time stays well under 0.05s per instance.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's local search accepts only strict max-KVPR decreases and only moves from the single worst GPU, so it is trapped in the first local minimum of a highly non-convex ratio objective. Annealing with a temperature schedule (T from ~initial max-KVPR/10 to ~1e-4, geometric decay) accepts occasional worsening moves, letting high req_rate/slo models migrate across memory-headroom gradients the incumbent's greedy seeds never explore. Candidate moves: (a) relocate one model to a random GPU, (b) swap two models between GPUs; reject if memory violated (hard constraint preserved by explicit `sum(size) ≤ GPU_MEM_SIZE` check before evaluation). Objective: max over GPUs of load/(mem − used), with used==mem treated as +inf. Keep best-ever feasible assignment; return it. Feasibility is guaranteed because every accepted state is memory-checked and the greedy seed is feasible (if greedy fails, raise as now). Expected-gain check: annealing's accepted-worsening moves explore assignment topologies the strict-descent incumbent provably cannot reach, so max KVPR should drop below 24.54; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 25.54 on the benchmark (i.e., 1/avg_max_KVPR strictly above the incumbent's).

strategies.title: [lp-bound-guided-repacking] Lower-bound-driven target-pressure rebalancing
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Analytic lower bound + constructive matching to per-GPU pressure targets (bin-packing-style decomposition)
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy-construction phase (the three ordering loop and `greedy()`); keep the incumbent's move/swap local search as the final polish.
Compute budget: One pass of bound computation + greedy-to-target construction (O(models × gpus) with a few ordering variants), then the existing local search; negligible added time.
Gain mechanism: Compute the LP-style lower bound L = (Σ req_rate/slo) / (gpus × GPU_MEM − Σ model_size) (total numerator over total free memory). The incumbent's greedy minimizes current KVPR per placement, which ignores the global target and systematically overloads early GPUs. Instead, assign models in descending req_rate/slo to the GPU whose *post-placement* KVPR is closest to (but preferably below) L, tie-breaking by largest free memory; this equalizes ratios toward the analytic optimum instead of greedily minimizing each step. Run this constructor for 3–4 orderings (req_rate/slo desc, req_rate/slo/size desc, size desc) and keep the feasible result with lowest max KVPR, then feed it to the incumbent's local search. Feasibility: only memory-fitting placements are made; if no GPU fits a model, fall back to the incumbent's best greedy result. Expected-gain check: the constructor targets the analytic lower bound L that the incumbent never computes, so the seeded max KVPR should approach L and after local search strictly undercut the incumbent's 24.54 max-KVPR; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 25.54.

strategies.title: [ejection-chain-relocation] Multi-model ejection chains from the bottleneck GPU
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: Ejection-chain / compound-move local search (deeper neighborhood than single move or pairwise swap)
Replacement scope: Replace the local-search block (the `improved` while-loop with single moves and pairwise swaps) with an ejection-chain search; keep the incumbent greedy construction as the seed.
Compute budget: Per iteration, chains of depth ≤ 4, at most ~500 chain evaluations per improvement round, cap total rounds at 50; expected time increase negligible (< 10 ms per instance).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can only move one model or swap two, so when the bottleneck GPU's excess cannot be relieved by any single feasible relocation (e.g., every other GPU lacks memory for the heavy model), it is permanently stuck. An ejection chain relocates model m1 from the worst GPU g to GPU h, and if h's KVPR then exceeds the target, cascades by ejecting m2 from h to another GPU, up to depth 4, accepting the whole chain only if the resulting global max KVPR strictly decreases and all intermediate states are memory-feasible. This compound-move topology reaches balanced configurations unreachable by 1-move/2-swap neighborhoods. Feasibility: every chain step checks `model_size ≤ free` on the destination before evaluation; the chain is applied only if the final state is fully feasible. Expected-gain check: compound relocations unlock bottleneck reductions that the incumbent's move/swap neighborhood provably cannot achieve when no single model fits elsewhere, so max KVPR should fall below the incumbent's; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 25.54.

strategies.title: [pairwise-swap-descent] Exhaustive best-improvement move+swap polish on the incu
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: pairwise-swap-descent
Replacement scope: Replace the post-SA reconstruction block in `compute_model_placement` (everything after `best_x, best` is finalized) with a deterministic first/best-improvement local search over the assignment vector; the SA loop itself is retained as the seed generator.
Compute budget: One deterministic pass structure: repeat sweeps of all n×(g−1) single-model moves and all n(n−1)/2 pairwise swaps until a full sweep yields no improvement, hard-capped at 20 full sweeps per instance. Each candidate evaluation is O(n). Expected added runtime ≪ current 0.24 s since n is small.
Gain mechanism: The SA acceptance is stochastic and terminates at a temperature where it can miss strictly improving 1-move/1-swap neighborhoods. An exhaustive deterministic descent over exactly those neighborhoods guarantees the returned solution is 1-swap/1-move local-optimal, which the incumbent does not guarantee. The new degree of freedom is exact enumeration of the complete move+swap neighborhood with an accept-only-if-max-KVPR-strictly-decreases criterion (memory feasibility checked per candidate). Fallback: if no improving move exists, output is unchanged, so score can only improve or stay equal; validity is preserved because every candidate assignment is memory-checked before acceptance and the final reconstruction places each model exactly once.
Expected-gain check: the falsifiable claim is that at least some of the 32 test instances have a strictly improving move or swap in the incumbent's SA output (evaluator threshold: raw max-KVPR mean strictly below the incumbent's, i.e., combined score > 26.255972), which the incumbent's stochastic terminal state cannot certify against.

strategies.title: [min-max-ratio-lagrangian] Bisection on the target KVPR with per-GPU knapsack-st
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: min-max-ratio-lagrangian
Replacement scope: Replace the entire construction phase (greedy, target_greedy, and the ordering loop) with a bisection search on the achievable max-KVPR value T; keep SA/local search only as an optional polish on the bisection result.
Compute budget: ≤ 40 bisection iterations, each doing a deterministic assignment pass (models sorted by weight descending, assigned to any GPU where they fit memory AND keep (load+w)/(mem−used−size) ≤ T, choosing the GPU with the largest resulting headroom); plus the retained SA polish capped at its current 20000 iterations. Net runtime comparable to incumbent.
Gain mechanism: The decision version of the problem is monotone: if max-KVPR T is achievable, any T′ > T is too, so bisection converges to the exact achievable optimum up to tolerance. The incumbent's target_greedy aims all GPUs at a single analytic LP bound L that ignores per-GPU memory asymmetry; bisection instead lets the effective per-GPU targets differ (a GPU with less free memory is allowed a tighter numerator budget), which is a genuinely different construction the incumbent cannot represent. Assignment per T is a greedy feasibility check: for each model (heaviest req_rate/slo first), pick the GPU that keeps its post-placement ratio ≤ T with maximum slack; if some model cannot be placed, T is infeasible. After bisection, take the best feasible T's placement. Feasibility invariant: each model assigned exactly once, memory checked at every step; if even T=∞ (pure first-fit) fails, fall back to the incumbent greedy result.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is per-GPU heterogeneous ratio targets under an exact monotone feasibility test, which the incumbent's single global LP target cannot express; falsifiable threshold: combined score > 26.255972 on the same 32-instance suite.

strategies.title: [population-crossover-search] Set-based evolutionary search with ratio-aware cro
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: population-crossover-search
Replacement scope: Replace the simulated-annealing block (both SA loops and the seeds machinery) with a population-based evolutionary search seeded by the existing greedy/target-greedy constructions; the construction phase is kept unchanged.
Compute budget: Population of 24 individuals, ≤ 300 generations; each generation does tournament selection, one crossover or mutation per offspring, and elitist retention. Per-candidate evaluation O(n). Bounded at ~7200 evaluations per instance, comparable to the current 40000 SA iterations but with fewer wasted infeasible samples.
Gain mechanism: SA explores a single trajectory and its swap move only exchanges two models' GPUs; a population with set-partition crossover combines whole GPU-load patterns from two good parents (e.g., for each GPU take the model subset from one parent, resolving duplicates by reassigning to the least-loaded feasible GPU), which is a structurally different recombination operator that can jump between basins the single-trajectory SA cannot reach in bounded time. Mutation is pressure-density-aware: pick a model on the current max-KVPR GPU and move it to the GPU minimizing the resulting max KVPR (best-of-moves rather than random move), so mutations are always objective-directed. Feasibility: every offspring is repaired by a first-fit pass on unassigned/overflowing models and discarded if repair fails; parents are always feasible, so the elite is always a valid placement covering each model exactly once. Determinism via fixed numpy seed.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is whole-basin recombination of feasible load patterns plus objective-directed mutation, neither of which the incumbent's single-trajectory random-walk SA possesses; falsifiable threshold: combined score > 26.255972 on the same suite, with the incumbent retained as fallback if the population converges worse.

Mechanism family: ruin-recreate-large-neighborhood (new family)
Replacement scop
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-recreate-large-neighborhood (new family)
Replacement scope: Replace the simulated-annealing phase (everything from "Simulated annealing over assignment vector" through the second SA loop) with a ruin-and-recreate loop seeded from the target-greedy incumbent.
Compute budget: 300 ruin-recreate iterations, each rebuilding at most ~30% of models via target-greedy; expected runtime ≤ current SA runtime (SA does 40k objective evaluations, this does ~300).
Gain mechanism: SA's single-move/swap neighborhood cannot restructure a whole GPU group at once; ruin-and-recreate removes a correlated subset (all models on 1–2 GPUs, or a random 25% sample) and reinserts them with the LP-bound target-greedy, letting the constructor re-optimize an entire sub-partition coherently. Accept if the new max-KVPR is ≤ current (or slightly worse with small annealing acceptance). Feasibility is guaranteed because reinsertion uses the same memory-checked target-greedy, and the incumbent is kept on any failure. This gives a structurally different escape direction than pointwise moves.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is correlated multi-model reinsertion (whole-GPU repacking), which the incumbent's single-element SA moves cannot realize; falsifiable threshold: avg max-KVPR strictly below the incumbent's on the same test suite (score > 26.255972).

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: lexicographic-tiebreak-descent (new family)
Replacement scope:
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lexicographic-tiebreak-descent (new family)
Replacement scope: Replace the SA objective function `objective(assign)` and the acceptance rule; keep the SA loop structure and all seeds as-is (this is the one permitted polish of the incumbent optimizer, but with a changed objective, not parameters).
Compute budget: same 20k+20k iteration budget as incumbent (no increase); runtime unchanged.
Gain mechanism: The current objective is only max-KVPR, so the search is blind on plateaus — thousands of states tie at the same max and SA wanders randomly. Use the lexicographic pair (max KVPR, second-max KVPR) — computed by partial-sorting the per-GPU ratios — as the objective, so moves that keep the max but lower the second-highest GPU are accepted. This directly builds toward states where reducing the bottleneck GPU's load is possible, because the second GPU is already prepared to absorb it. Feasibility unchanged (same memory rejection). Strictly more accepting than incumbent on plateaus, never worse (lexicographic comparison reduces to the same max when max changes).
Expected-gain check: the corrected bottleneck is plateau blindness — the incumbent accepts ties with probability via temperature only, while the lexicographic objective makes every second-max-reducing move a strict improvement; falsifiable threshold: score > 26.255972 on the fixed test suite.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: quota-decomposition-assignment (new family)
Replacement scope:
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: quota-decomposition-assignment (new family)
Replacement scope: Replace the construction phase (target_greedy and its ordering loop) with a two-stage deterministic constructor: (1) compute per-GPU free memory under a first-fit-decreasing size packing, (2) solve a small transportation-style assignment of models to GPU load-quota buckets.
Compute budget: one deterministic construction plus one greedy-repair pass; ≤ O(n·g) work, negligible runtime; then hand off to the incumbent SA/lexicographic polish.
Gain mechanism: The LP bound L assumes uniform free memory per GPU, but after packing, GPUs have heterogeneous headroom f_g. The true equalized optimum sets per-GPU load W_g = L·f_g (load proportional to headroom), not equal load. Stage 1 packs sizes FFD to maximize and equalize total headroom feasibility; stage 2 assigns models greedily (by weight descending) to the GPU minimizing |load_g + w − L·f_g| subject to memory fit, with a repair pass that relocates any oversized assignment. This targets the exact first-order optimality condition Σw_g/f_g equalized, which the incumbent's symmetric target-greedy only approximates; memory feasibility is enforced at every insertion, with the plain-greedy result kept as fallback if any stage fails.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is per-GPU heterogeneous load quotas (W_g ∝ f_g) derived from the analytic equalization condition, which the incumbent's uniform-L target cannot express; falsifiable threshold: score > 26.255972 on the fixed test suite.

This directly builds toward states where reducing the bottleneck GPU's load is possible, because the second GPU is already prepared to absorb it. Feasibility unchanged (same memory rejection). Strictly more accepting than incumbent on plateaus, never worse (lexicographic comparison reduces to the same max when max changes).
Expected-gain check: the corrected bottleneck is plateau blindness — the incumbent accepts ties with probability via temperature only, while the lexicographic objective makes every second-max-reducing move a strict improvement; falsifiable threshold: score > 26.255972 on the fixed test suite.

strategies.title: [bottleneck-targeted-binary-search] Threshold-feasibility packing at a target KV
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: threshold-bisection-feasibility
Replacement scope: Replace the entire SA phase (everything after `best = (p, cur_max, load, free)` selection) with a bisection loop; keep the greedy/target-greedy constructors only as the initial upper bound and feasibility fallback.
Compute budget: At most 40 bisection iterations; each iteration solves one decision problem via first-fit-decreasing feasibility check over at most n×gpu_num candidate placements — total O(40·n·g), well under current SA's 20000 iterations. Expected runtime ≤ current 0.24 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent optimizes the max-KVPR only indirectly through stochastic moves. This strategy directly attacks the decision form: "can all models be placed so every GPU's KVPR ≤ T?" For a candidate T, a model with weight w can go on GPU g only if `(load_g + w)/(free_g - size) ≤ T`, i.e. `w ≤ T·free_g - (T+1)·size... ` precisely: `load_g + w ≤ T·(MEM - used_g - size)`. Bisection on T between the LP lower bound L and the greedy incumbent value converges to the smallest achievable T, which by construction is ≤ the incumbent's value (the greedy solution certifies feasibility at the incumbent T). Each feasibility check uses FFD: sort models by weight descending, assign each to the GPU with most remaining "T-slack" `T·(MEM - used_g) - load_g - (T+... )` that still admits it; if any model fails, T is infeasible. This is a genuinely new degree of freedom — the incumbent never uses the per-GPU T-dependent admission constraint `w ≤ T·(MEM−used_g−size) − load_g`, which is the exact structural condition the optimum must satisfy, and it converts the non-linear ratio objective into a linear-per-GPU knapsack-style decision. Hard constraints preserved: every model is assigned exactly once and memory is enforced inside the admission test; the final feasible solution found at the smallest feasible T is returned, with the greedy incumbent kept as fallback if bisection finds none better.
Expected-gain check: The returned solution's max KVPR is at most the smallest T for which FFD feasibility succeeds, and FFD is exact-feasible at T = incumbent value (the greedy solution itself witnesses this), so the result is ≤ incumbent max-KVPR 25.256 with strict improvement whenever FFD packs tighter than greedy at some T below the incumbent value — a falsifiable evaluator threshold of any combined_score > 26.256.

strategies.title: [complete-kernel-enumeration] Exhaustive optimal placement for small instances v
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: exact-branch-and-bound
Replacement scope: Replace the whole SA phase; keep greedy constructors as the initial upper bound feeding the bound-pruning.
Compute budget: Branch-and-bound over model→GPU assignments with node cap 200,000 per instance; abort and return best-found when cap hit. Expected runtime ≤ 0.3 s for typical benchmark sizes (n ≤ ~20).
Gain mechanism: For the benchmark's small instances, the true optimum is reachable by systematic search — a degree of freedom the incumbent's stochastic SA cannot guarantee. Order models by weight (req_rate/slo) descending; maintain per-GPU (load, used) arrays; at each node try each GPU for the next model, pruning a branch when (a) memory exceeded, or (b) the optimistic bound `max(current_max_kvpr, L)` ≥ best-so-far, where L is the LP bound `total_load/total_free` computed on remaining unassigned models and remaining free memory — a valid lower bound since remaining load must fit in remaining headroom. Additional prune: if placing the model on GPU g makes its KVPR ≥ best-so-far, skip. Because the objective is min-max, once any single GPU's KVPR reaches the incumbent value the entire subtree is dead, giving strong pruning. Feasibility is enforced structurally (memory check at every node, every model assigned at leaves). The greedy incumbent remains the fallback upper bound, so the result is never worse. This differs from all spent families: it is deterministic exhaustive search with admissible bounds, not a local move/swap/anneal/crossover neighborhood.
Expected-gain check: Branch-and-bound returns a proven-optimal-or-better-than-greedy assignment, so max-KVPR ≤ incumbent 25.256 with strict gain whenever greedy/SA is suboptimal on any test instance — falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 26.256, with the gain mechanism (exhaustive search with LP-bound pruning) unavailable to the incumbent's stochastic neighborhood.

strategies.title: [pressure-flow-rebalancing] Successive min-max redistribution via bottleneck-GPU
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: max-flow-style-offload-rebalance
Replacement scope: Replace the SA loop; keep greedy/target-greedy construction as the starting solution and fallback.
Compute budget: At most 500 relocation rounds, each scanning at most n×gpu_num candidate moves — ≤ 500·n·g evaluations, comparable to one SA run. Expected runtime ≈ 0.1 s.
Gain mechanism: New topology: instead of random perturbations, each round identifies the unique bottleneck GPU b (max KVPR) and tries to *drain* it — for each model i on b, compute the resulting KVPR of b and of every target GPU g if i moves there (memory permitting); accept the move minimizing `max(kvpr_b_after, kvpr_g_after, second_highest_kvpr)` — i.e., a lexicographic drain objective that specifically collapses the current maximum rather than any random objective. After each accepted move, recompute the bottleneck and repeat; when no single move reduces the max, try 2-chains (move i from b to g, then move j from g to a third GPU h) with the same acceptance test, bounded to one chain per round. This is a targeted, deterministic escape direction the incumbent lacks: SA's random single-element moves almost never find the coordinated (move i, then move j) pair that relieves a bottleneck, whereas the chain construction enumerates them directly. Feasibility: memory checked before every move; every assignment remains a complete partition; incumbent returned if no round improves. Distinct from pairwise-swap-descent (spent): that family swapped between arbitrary GPUs against the global objective; this drains the *current bottleneck only* and uses 2-chains, a different neighborhood topology.
Expected-gain check: Each accepted round strictly reduces the global max KVPR (acceptance test is strict lexicographic improvement on the max), so the final max-KVPR ≤ greedy incumbent's 25.256, with strict gain whenever a bottleneck-relieving move or 2-chain exists that SA missed — falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 26.256.
